declaration_name: Clarence Valley NSW Bushfires, 21 January – 13 February 2024
main_fires: Sandon River fire (4,330 ha); Lake Arragan fire (574 ha); Burragan Rd Coutts Crossing; Gwydir Hwy Jackadgery
towns_affected: Sandon River, Lake Arragan area, Wooli/Minnie Water, Coutts Crossing, Jackadgery
summary: In late January 2024 lightning-started fires burned through the Sandon River and Lake Arragan areas of Clarence Valley LGA on the NSW mid-north coast, together covering roughly 4,900 ha of bushland including sections of Yuraygir and other coastal reserves near Wooli and Minnie Water. Coverage located in this search (ABC Emergency incident pages, ABC News item on aircraft fighting the Wooli/Minnie Water fire) confirms the fire perimeter and an Advice-level bushfire status through late January, but no news report giving verified counts of homes destroyed/damaged was found. The declaration remained active to 13 February 2024, covering the wider Clarence Valley LGA.

General web search repeatedly surfaced coverage of an unrelated, larger Tenterfield fire complex from October–November 2023 (Sawyers Creek/Benders Creek, ~24,000 ha) rather than this September 2024 event, so no verified news facts (homes destroyed, evacuations) specific to the 2024 fire were confirmed in this pass; this is flagged as a caveat rather than reported as zero impact.

main_fires: Sandstone Caves fire (6,465 ha); Wyuna fire, Oxley Hwy (62 ha); Bogans Well Rd (25 ha)
summary: The Sandstone Caves fire, reported near Dandry in the Pilliga Nature Reserve (Warrumbungle LGA) from about 3:40pm on 26 February 2025, grew rapidly — reaching roughly 1,060 ha by that evening and eventually about 6,500 ha before containment — and closed sections of the Newell Highway. NSW RFS opened a Bush Fire Information Point at Coonabarabran Post Office on 3 March 2025 for affected residents, indicating community impact, but no verified figures for homes destroyed/damaged were located in this search. This was the largest-area event in the group.

declaration_name: Central Coast Bushfires from 6 December 2025
summary: A fast-moving bushfire that began in parkland at Koolewong around 12:40pm on 6 December 2025 escalated within hours to an Emergency Warning, destroying 16 homes and damaging a further 9, plus 7 outbuildings destroyed, according to ABC News (7–8 December 2025). About 60 people used the Gosford RSL as an evacuation centre. It occurred amid a state-wide extreme heat/fire-danger day on which more than 50–75 fires were burning across NSW. This was the most heavily documented and highest-impact event in the group.

No specific home-loss count for Lake Macquarie itself was published in the ministerial release.
